business_scope.primary_industry_name: Franchise Licensing and Syrups Supply Chain for Bubble Tea Chains

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law tradition with customary law elements and US-inspired corporate statutes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association with the United States of America (investment, trade, and economic assistance framework)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus) — trade and services framework
No comprehensive bilateral investment treaty or double taxation agreement specifically identified as in force for the Marshall Islands at this due diligence stage

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The Business Corporation Act, Title 27, RMI Code 2011, as amended; the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2012, as amended; the Marshall Islands Beneficial Ownership Information (Private) Registration Regulations; and the Financial Action Task Force-aligned guidance issued by the Financial Intelligence Office of the Republic of the Marshall Islands.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporator together with notary public in the country of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization at a Marshall Islands consulate for non-Hague countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport for each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or notary public in each individual's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for any corporate shareholder or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the corporate shareholder or UBO

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Principal shareholder resolution or consent approving the RMI Business Corporation formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered office or corporate secretary of the corporate shareholder

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, United Kingdom HMT Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, RMI domestic sanctions/designation notices, and global PEP databases before engagement. Enhanced due diligence and source-of-funds verification are mandatory for any politically exposed person, higher-risk jurisdiction, or sanctions-linked nexus, in accordance with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2012.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RMI Registrar of Corporations — Marshall Islands Company Registry Name Reservation System (name clearance is submitted through licensed RMI registered agents using the official Registry Name Reservation interface and public search)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English using Latin characters. Foreign-script names are not accepted unless transliterated into English. The name must end with 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or an accepted abbreviation such as 'Corp.', 'Inc.', or 'Ltd.', and must be distinguishable from names of existing RMI companies, foreign registered companies, and all Registry-approved reserved names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Before expiry, the applicant may file a written extension request with the RMI Registrar of Corporations; upon payment of the applicable extension fee, the reservation may be extended for one additional 30-day period. If the name is rejected, a written formal reconsideration request must be filed with the Registrar of Corporations within 14 days of the rejection notice, annexing the name-search report and a comparison of similar registered names. If the reconsideration is denied, an administrative appeal or judicial review may be filed in the High Court of the Republic of the Marshall Islands within 30 days of the denial through a locally licensed attorney.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or non-operational office is permitted only where the statutory registered office is provided by a licensed RMI registered agent maintaining a physical, staffed office in Majuro and accepting service of process. A virtual-only office without a licensed RMI registered agent is not permitted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 2% for a standard non-resident, tax-exempt Business Corporation holding franchise licensing and syrup supply-chain IP; 45% if economic substance filing indicates any RMI-sourced activity or requires a RMI business/trade license

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (BCA), Title 24 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code, Sections 9 (Incorporation), 10 (Articles of Incorporation), 35 (Directors), 39 (Officers), and 52 (Registered Office and Agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Chief Registrar, Ministry of Finance and Administration, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Certificate of Incorporation issued upon acceptance)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow deposit or capital commitment required for non-resident business corporations; working capital may be introduced via shareholder loans or contributed surplus as resolved by the board
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation filed with the Registrar of Corporations are hereby ratified and adopted. The board approves the issuance of 1,000,000 common shares, no par value, to the founding shareholder at a subscription price of USD 0.001 per share. The registered office at the address of the licensed registered agent is adopted for service of process. The following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary. The board authorizes such officers to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and complete all licensing applications. This resolution is effective immediately and recorded in the corporate minute book. Certified by the Corporate Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Online Name Reservation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application for 'Boba Tea Global Franchise, Inc.' or a distinguishing variant. Confirm the name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing corporate names in the RMI register. Pay the filing fee and receive the name reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Identification of the beneficial owner and incorporator
Filing fee receipt for the name reservation (USD 20)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit a revised name reservation with additional distinguishing words, or file an administrative appeal to the Chief Registrar within 5 business days of the rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered local law firm / notary public authorized under RMI law
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in English, stating the corporate name, registered agent details, share structure, board composition, and permitted business purposes. Have the incorporator sign the articles before a notary public. Attach the name reservation certificate.
required_dossiers: Signed and notarized Articles of Incorporation
Name reservation certificate
Consent to act as registered agent from the RMI registered agent
Identity documents of the incorporator and initial directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar identifies a deficiency, amend the articles and resubmit within 14 days. If the registered agent consent is defective, obtain a corrected consent and file a supplemental statement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Payment of Incorporation Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Articles of Incorporation through a registered agent or e-filing portal. Pay the incorporation fee and stamp duty using a certified bank draft or authorized electronic payment. Upon acceptance, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Payment receipt for statutory filing fee (USD 200)
Cover letter from the registered agent
Certificate of name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, provide a written response to the Registrar detailing the curative amendment, pay any outstanding fee, and request expedited re-review. If the certificate is denied, apply to the RMI Superior Court for a writ of mandamus.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Registered Agent Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the appointment of a licensed registered agent in the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the physical address of the registered office. File the registered agent acceptance form and the notice of registered office concurrently with the Articles or within 5 business days of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Registered agent acceptance and consent
Notice of registered office address
Certificate of Incorporation (attached as proof)
Registered agent license number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent appointment is rejected, appoint a substitute licensed agent and file an amended notice. If the physical address is non-deliverable, provide a corrected street address and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (minutes executed in RMI or by written consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct the organizational meeting or execute a unanimous written consent resolving the adoption of bylaws, approval of share issuance, appointment of officers, selection of the bank, and authorization of license applications. File the executed resolutions in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Organizational meeting minutes or unanimous written consent
Bylaws of the corporation
Share subscription agreement and payment evidence
Indemnification agreements for directors and officers
Full name and addresses of officers and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the corporate records, cure by filing a supplementary statement and confirm the resolution date. If the quorum was deficient, re-execute the resolutions with the required director majority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Marshall Islands Foreign Investment Board (FIB), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Trade; Business License Office, Ministry of Finance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Employment License / Trade, Manufacturing and Franchise Operations License

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA), Republic of the Marshall Islands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class II – Environmental Compliance Registration (as the activity is a low-risk food and beverage syrup packaging and franchise licensing operation with no major discharges)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must conform to EPA concentration limits for BOD (25 mg/L), TSS (35 mg/L), pH (6.0-9.0), and oil & grease (10 mg/L). VOCs and refrigerants are subject to standards promulgated under the RMI Ozone Depleting Substances Regulations. Solid waste handling must comply with national waste management rules and may require a waste handling permit for syrup containers and packaging.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance for storage and warehousing of syrups, certificate of structural load inspection for bottling equipment areas, and occupational safety clearance under the RMI Occupational Safety and Health Act; premises must have fire extinguishers, emergency egress, and a workplace health checklist certified by the National Fire Authority and the Ministry of Health and Human Services.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenue and Taxation Office, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands; official government portal: https://rmi.gov.mh
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident Business Corporation (BC) incorporated under the Business Corporations Act 1990 is not issued an RMI Tax Identification Number at incorporation and is not required to procure one unless it derives income sourced within the Republic of the Marshall Islands. The Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar of Corporations serves as the statutory identifier for the entity. If a domestic tax obligation arises (e.g., payroll withholding for local employees or withholding tax on RMI-source payments), the BC must register for a TIN with the Revenue and Taxation Office by submitting the prescribed application form, supporting certificate of incorporation, and evidence of a local registered agent; registration is activated within 5–10 business days. A BC with no RMI-source income remains outside the assessed income tax net with no TIN requirement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: Non-Resident Business Corporation treated as tax-exempt on income derived from sources outside the Republic of the Marshall Islands; territorial source taxation applies only to assessed income from RMI sources. Domestic-source income of a non-resident BC is generally subject to a 3% final withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, rents and other specified income; the entity is not liable to corporate income tax on foreign franchise royalties, syrup export sales or offshore management fees.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or analogous entity-classification election exists under Marshall Islands law; classification is fixed by the statutory form of the Business Corporation. No hybrid mismatch elections are available under the Income Tax Act 1989. The non-resident tax exemption is self-executing under the Business Corporations Act and does not require an advance ruling; however, a taxpayer may request a private interpretation from the Revenue and Taxation Office to confirm sourcing and exemption treatment. RMI is an Inclusive Framework member; no Action 2 hybrid-mismatch election mechanism has been domesticated.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable: no VAT/GST/sales-and-use tax registration regime exists in the Republic of the Marshall Islands. The only material indirect levy is customs import duty under the Customs and Tariff Act 1990, imposed at the point of importation at a standard ad valorem rate of up to 10% on CIF value; recurring importers register with the Customs Service for an importer code, but there is no economic-nexus turnover threshold. Exports and offshore services are outside the indirect tax base.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. No electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, API-based tax filing, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control regime is mandated by the Revenue and Taxation Office. Customs formalities for import and export physical clearances are processed through written or digital declarations submitted to the Customs Service of the Marshall Islands; standard commercial invoices and packing lists suffice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: De facto 0% export rate: since the Marshall Islands imposes no VAT/GST, exports of goods (including syrup and beverage concentrate) and offshore franchise services are inherently outside the scope of indirect tax, with no registration or zero-rating claim procedure required. For income-tax purposes, a non-resident Business Corporation is exempt from RMI tax on gross revenue derived from exports and offshore services because such income is not sourced in the Republic of the Marshall Islands; eligibility requires that the supply of goods concludes at export (FOB Majuro or other RMI port) and that franchise royalty services are performed entirely outside RMI or are attributable to foreign franchisees.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (RMI Customs Service export entry)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank FX receipt evidencing receipt of foreign currency proceeds
Certificate of Incorporation of the non-resident Business Corporation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No export zero-rating or VAT refund regime exists in RMI, hence no VAT clawback mechanism arises. However, material misstatements in customs declarations are subject to the penalties of the Customs and Tariff Act, including fines, seizure and forfeiture of goods. Misrepresentations made to the Revenue and Taxation Office with intent to sustain the non-resident exemption, when the income is in fact RMI-source, can void the exemption and retroactively expose the BC to assessed income tax, gross revenue tax where applicable, the 3% withholding tax, late-payment interest, penalties up to the amount of the underpaid tax, and criminal liability for fraudulent filing.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commissioner, Republic of the Marshall Islands (under the Banking Act 1987 and Ministry of Finance); no RMI central bank exists — the United States Federal Reserve System is the de facto monetary and clearing authority because the US dollar is the sole legal tender pursuant to the Compact of Free Association.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Freedom of convertibility is absolute by design: the official currency of the RMI is the US dollar, so there is no local exchange rate to administer and no current-account or capital-account restriction. Profits, dividends, royalties, and liquidation proceeds are freely remittable from the RMI without exchange approval, provided the corporate record is clean (audited financial statements, beneficial-ownership declaration, and tax-compliance confirmation). The only practical friction is global correspondent-bank de-risking arising from RMI's offshore-flag profile, which elevates document burdens but does not constitute a legal convertibility barrier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. The RMI has no foreign-exchange-control law, no export-proceeds surrender timeline, and no mandatory conversion ratio because the US dollar is legal tender. All export receipts (including franchise royalties and syrup-supply proceeds) are retained and settled in USD without obligation to repatriate or convert; however, remittances remain subject to OFAC screening and standard correspondent-bank monitoring under the RMI's Compact-relationship obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam (Republic of the Marshall Islands Branch)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Clearing Account and Trade-Finance Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. The RMI has no electronic-money-institution licensing framework, and major overseas digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business) generally decline onboarding of RMI-registered holding entities because of correspondent-bank de-risking, jurisdictional reputation concerns, and the absence of a native EMI license. The RMI's earlier SOV digital-currency project is not an operational payment rail. Digital EMIs may serve only as ancillary collection conduits in operating countries after a physical RMI banking relationship is established; they must not carry core franchise-royalty or syrup-procurement clearing flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for first-time corporate account opening at both tier-1 banks. Directors, or at minimum the designated signatories acting under a certified board resolution, must appear in person in Majuro for an interview, original-notarized signature verification, and witness of the corporate seal. No fully electronic e-KYC or video-identification onboarding is codified under RMI law; a remote opening is possible only as a discretionary exception where a regulated RMI corporate service provider with a physical office completes the identity attestation and the bank's compliance committee approves or a pre-verified shareholder record exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name-match and jurisdictional-risk screening flagging RMI's offshore-flag status, tax-haven press references, and prior Paradise Papers associative media coverage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing issued by the RMI Registrar; certified charter and current bylaws; board resolution designating signatories and account purpose; corporate-service-provider due-diligence file; OFAC and FATCA-compliant negative-media search report from a recognized screening provider; group-structure chart proving a real ISIC 5610 franchise business with executed master franchise agreements and syrup-supply contracts; and formal confirmation of tax-exemption or tax-clearance status from the RMI Ministry of Finance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity where the ultimate beneficial owner is a non-US resident or where nominee-shareholder arrangements obscure control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed beneficial-ownership declaration consistent with the RMI Business Corporations Act and the bank's beneficial-ownership register; certified passport copies and proof of physical address for every UBO; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation (bank statements, audited financial statements, franchise-licensing revenue stream evidence); KYC certification by a licensed RMI trust-and-company-service provider; and an express written confirmation that the entity is an operating franchisor and not a financial-services vehicle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Correspondent-bank de-risking concern triggered by anticipated high-frequency USD wire flows and a low physical footprint in the RMI.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed 24-month business plan and cash-flow model; schedule of franchised-store locations; sample royalty invoices and syrup-supply purchase orders; copy of the global-franchise disclosure document; counterparty risk summary confirming no sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions; commitment to maintain a minimum compensating balance at BOMI or Bank of Guam; and three years of audited financial statements, or interim carve-out audited statements for the recently formed entity, demonstrating traceable economic substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections to the RMI entity are executed by SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers drawn on the parent or investor's bank and routed through the US Federal Reserve clearing system (Fedwire/CHIPS) to BOMI or Bank of Guam. All transfers must be denominated in USD to avoid conversion friction; non-USD injections are converted at the correspondent bank's commercial rate with the purpose code indicated on the wire. Use OECD Balance-of-Payments purpose codes — 'C' for capital transfers (equity injection) or 'F' for intercompany financial loans — and include the FAO account reference, underlying board-resolution reference, and the stamped filing number of the RMI business corporation. Pre-submission of the corporate resolution, source-of-funds statement, and group-structure chart is required so that the receiving bank can clear OFAC screening and complete the compliance hold prior to crediting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for franchise-royalty wires and syrup-supply-chain settlements are cleared through SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers; bank-to-bank reimbursements for letters of credit use SWIFT MT202 COV. Commercial letters of credit for syrup-container or equipment purchases are issued by BOMI or Bank of Guam with advising and confirming banks in the operating jurisdictions, using USD as the settlement currency. Payments to franchise operators in foreign markets are consolidated through the RMI treasury account and routed to local clearing systems (e.g., ACH, Faster Payments, CIPS) only after conversion via the in-country dealer bank; Local POS receipts at franchised stores are collected locally and swept periodically into the RMI treasury via pooled-account or master-franchise settlement structures rather than through direct RMI POS rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD/foreign-currency FX forwards executed through US or Asian dealer banks to hedge franchise-royalty and syrup-procurement exposure
Cross-currency basis swaps (USD vs operating-country currency) for long-term intercompany financing and dividend-repatriation exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted or less-liquid currencies (e.g., offshore CNY or VND) executed through dealer banks outside the restricted jurisdiction
Plain-vanilla FX options (call/put, vanilla European-style) for downside protection on committed franchise capital expenditure flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report and Annual Franchise Tax Payment (Business Corporations Act, Section 106)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Registrar, Republic of the Marshall Islands
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing window opens January 1 and closes June 30 of each calendar year; report and franchise tax due on or before June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of US$100 or 10% of the assessed franchise tax, whichever is greater, plus 1% monthly interest on unpaid tax; failure to file for two successive years authorizes the Registrar to administratively dissolve the corporation and strike its name from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership and Registered Details Refresh (Corporate Registered Agents Regulations, 2016)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Resident Agent (records maintained on behalf of the Registrar; not a public registry filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually at each annual review and promptly upon any share transfer or change of directors, members, or registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-response permits the resident agent to resign; a corporation without a resident agent for 30 days is subject to administrative dissolution by the Registrar.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None for a non-resident Business Corporation. The Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act imposes no mandatory independent audit and no financial statement filing on non-resident domestic corporations; an audit is triggered only by the articles of incorporation, bylaws, shareholder resolution, lender covenant, or special-statute licensing activity conducted inside the Republic.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutorily prescribed accounting framework for non-resident BCs; books are customarily maintained under IFRS or US GAAP, and audited statements, if any, are prepared under the adopted framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Marshall Islands Corporate Registered Agents Regulations, the licensed resident agent must obtain and maintain adequate, current beneficial ownership information and refresh or confirm that information at least annually and upon each share transfer or change in control. The confirmation remains in the agent's private records and is not filed in any public UBO register; the Register of Members must be updated contemporaneously with each transfer to support the agent's verification.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$800 – US$2,000 per annum (typical licensed RMI registered agent and registered office fee for a non-resident Business Corporation)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$0 statutory (no mandatory audit); voluntary certified audit for lender or franchise-investor purposes typically US$5,000 – US$15,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% — the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) imposes no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, and no branch profits tax on Business Corporations (BC). The only revenue-based impost is the Gross Revenue Tax (GRT) Act 1989, applied at 3% exclusively to revenues sourced in the RMI.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: De facto 0% effective rate for non-resident BCs because franchise royalty, syrup supply-chain, and IP licensing income from overseas franchisees has no RMI nexus. Existing GRT exemptions: charitable, educational, cooperative enterprises. No export-processing zone regime, no royalty deduction cap, no net-operating-loss mechanics exist because no income tax base exists.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Report and Franchise Tax Declaration (BCA Form AR), filed via the RMI Registrar of Corporations e-filing portal at https://eservices.register-rmi.com (managed by the RMI Office of the Registrar, Majuro). No corporate income tax return exists; the AR serves as the combined statutory annual filing, franchise-tax return and good-standing certificate.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing window opens on January 1 and closes on September 30 of each calendar year, covering the immediately preceding calendar year. Newly incorporated BCs file their first AR in the first full window following incorporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact corporate name, English-language legal form, and RMI registration number, matching the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the legal name exactly as registered; never use a trade name or DBA without a registered name-change amendment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Date of Certificate of Incorporation; jurisdiction is RMI (domestic business corporation).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident status does not alter the domestic incorporation fact; state the RMI incorporation date only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Street address of the registered office in Majuro — the licensed registered agent's physical address (a PO Box alone is invalid).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must equal the registered agent's RMI address exactly; the agent maintains the corporate records and service-of-process point.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of authorized shares, par value per share, and classes of stock as stated in Articles, e.g., 50,000 ordinary shares at USD 0.01.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the issued and authorized amounts from the capital table; increases, stock splits, or class changes require prior BCA amendment filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and addresses of all persons serving as directors (minimum one, no nationality requirement).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nominee directors are permitted but must not be used to conceal beneficial ownership; each director's full residential address is required for the beneficial-ownership register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and addresses of President, Secretary, and Treasurer, or a declaration that the office is vacant.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If management is carried on by a Hong Kong or US franchise parent, the parent's officers may hold these offices; report the foreign street address, not the RMI agent address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, license number, and signature of the licensed RMI Registered Agent undertaking service of process and record-keeping.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The agent must be a licensed RMI resident agent under BCA Article 12; the agent's countersignature is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 (Principal Business Address and GRT Affiliation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal place of business worldwide; confirmation of whether any gross revenue was derived from RMI sources.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the global headquarters (e.g., the franchise HQ in Hong Kong/US); tick 'No RMI-source revenue' to avoid GRT registration; RMI-source sales (e.g., syrup delivered to a Majuro store) require separate GRT registration and monthly returns.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory franchise tax computed on authorized shares per BCA Section 76: ≤5,000 shares = USD 250; 5,001–10,000 = USD 500; 10,001–20,000 = USD 750; 20,001–50,000 = USD 1,000; rising progressively to a USD 10,000 cap at >100,000,000 shares.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident BCs pay the identical sliding scale; no reduced rate or minimum franchise-tax waiver exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the register of beneficial owners (Form BO-1) is physically maintained at the registered agent's office and identifies all individuals owning >25%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The final beneficial owner of the global boba franchise group (the natural person controlling the franchise chain) must be disclosed; failure is a criminal offense, not a mere filing defect.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: flat USD 100 penalty immediately after September 30. Unpaid franchise tax: 1.5% monthly interest compounded. Persistent delinquency for two consecutive years triggers Registrar's notice of dissolution; three years triggers involuntary dissolution and loss of corporate name. Reinstatement costs: all arrears, penalties, legalization fees, and a USD 250 reinstatement fee; any contract completed while dissolved is voidable at counterparty election.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — RMI imposes no withholding tax on dividends, regardless of the shareholder's residence. Dividends declared by MH_BC to franchise-group shareholders exit RMI free of any WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No double-tax treaty network exists for RMI; the RMI is not a contracting party to any comprehensive OECD or UN model income-tax treaty and does not issue income-tax residency certificates (TRCs). Administrative protocol for cross-border transactions: (1) certify good standing through the RMI Registrar's Certificate of Good Standing (dated within 90 days); (2) obtain a certified extract of the BO-1 beneficial-ownership register; (3) furnish the counterparty's payer with IRS Form W-8BEN-E (US), UK CH-29, or equivalent for jurisdictions requiring proof of foreign status; (4) invoke treaty relief only in the payer's jurisdiction where a treaty between the payer's country and the ultimate tax-resident parent exists — the RMI entity cannot itself be the claimant of treaty benefits absent any RMI DTA; (5) apply reduced WHT via the foreign payer's normal treaty-relief forms, attaching the RMI Certificate of Incorporation and proving the absence of an RMI permanent establishment to avoid ECI / PE exposure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Outbound (paid by MH_BC): 0% statutory WHT on royalties and 0% on interest under RMI law. Inbound (royalties/interest paid to MH_BC by franchisees): foreign-source income, not taxable in RMI. RMI-source royalties (rare; e.g., a Majuro franchisee paying MH_BC for trademark license) are subject to the 3% GRT collected by withholding. US-source royalties paid to MH_BC attract 30% US statutory WHT under IRC 881(a) because no US-RMI treaty exists. US-source portfolio interest paid to MH_BC benefits from the IRC 881(c) exemption if the obligation is in registered form, MH_BC files a valid Form W-8BEN-E, and it is not a bank within IRC 881(c)(3)(A).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No local TP legislation or documentation threshold exists because RMI levies no income tax. The OECD country-by-country reporting (CbCR) threshold applies only to the ultimate parent jurisdiction of the global boba tea franchise group: when consolidated group revenue ≥ USD 750,000,000, a CbCR filing obligation arises in the group's parent jurisdiction, with MH_BC serving as a constituent entity. Local File and Master File obligations arise, if at all, in the tax jurisdictions of franchisees and the operational parent — not in the RMI. Recommended practicum: maintain a group transfer-pricing policy (royalty 3–6% of franchisee net sales, syrup gross margin 35–55%, management-fee mark-up 5–10% cost-plus) to withstand audits in paying jurisdictions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: RMI does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime equivalent to BVI/Cayman. However, the OECD BEPS Inclusive Framework substantial-activity requirement for geographically mobile IP income applies de facto: an RMI BC holding the boba-tea trademark and syrup formula must demonstrate core income-generating activities (strategic decisions, IP development, risk management) where the actual personnel are based (e.g., the Hong Kong franchise headquarters). The RMI Nonresident Domestic Corporation regime imposes an annual 0% tax status but requires that no business be conducted inside the RMI. The EU currently lists the RMI as a non-cooperative jurisdiction for tax purposes, meaning franchisee jurisdictions will apply heightened substance review and conduit-company scrutiny. Practical substance protocol: board meetings physically held in Hong Kong, executed minutes, employment contracts and payroll of the syrup R&D team, and beneficial-ownership transparency at the RMI agent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Statements to the Registrar (Corporate Fraud)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing an Annual Report with false information — understated authorized shares to cut franchise tax, fictitious director identities, or undisclosed 25%+ beneficial owners of the boba tea franchise chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: BCA Section 68: criminal penalty of up to USD 10,000 fine and/or up to five years' imprisonment per false statement; administrative revocation of good standing; involuntary dissolution; directors disqualified from acting as corporate officers in the RMI.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced for statutory fraud: each signing director is jointly and severally liable for the full franchise-tax deficiency, treble damages under civil fraud, and counterparty reliance losses; RMI courts may issue asset-freezing orders and travel bans pending trial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Gross Revenue Tax Evasion on RMI-Source Sales
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling syrup, boba supplies, or franchise rights into the Republic of the Marshall Islands (e.g., a Majuro store supplied by MH_BC) without registering under the GRT Act and remitting the 3% gross revenue tax, or falsifying monthly GRT returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Gross Revenue Tax Act 1989: fine up to USD 10,000, imprisonment up to five years, plus civil assessment of three times the unpaid tax and automatic 10% late surcharge and 1% monthly interest; the RMI Tax Information Authority may suspend the business license of any RMI franchisee involved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who directed the underdeclaration are personally liable for the treble civil assessment; criminal convictions carry a personal restitution order and, under the Compact of Free Association extradition framework, a travel ban enforceable upon departure from the US or RMI.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Conduit / Shell Arrangement and BEPS Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Channeling boba-tea royalty income from franchisees through MH_BC solely to strip profits into a zero-tax jurisdiction, while all substantive IP management is performed abroad and the RMI entity lacks personnel, contracts, and bank-account decision rights.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: No RMI penalty (no local income tax); but franchisee-source tax authorities may impose withholding deficiencies of up to 30% on gross royalties, together with interest and penalties of up to 100% of the tax, and the EU listing of RMI triggers defensive anti-abuse rules in EU member states; the entity may be denied GRT/good-standing certifications for misuse of the non-resident status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foreign GAAR/CFC litigation exposes directors who signed certificates of residence or substance to civil breach-of-duty claims; if personal guarantees back the franchise agreements, directors face direct collection on audit adjustments; RMI BCA § 61 indemnification does not cover willful participation in sham structures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the global franchise payment rails (wire transfers of franchise royalties) without maintaining the Form BO-1 beneficial-ownership register at the RMI registered agent, or accepting franchise payments from sanctioned / PEP-linked storefronts without customer due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RMI Beneficial Ownership Act 2020 and Money Laundering Regulations: corporate fine up to USD 500,000; directors' and officers' fines up to USD 100,000 and imprisonment up to ten years; the registered agent may be struck off and the corporation's certificate of registration suspended for 12 months.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML obligations attach personally to each director and compliance officer; personal assets are directly attachable for civil penalties; criminal conviction leads to 10-year imprisonment and exclusion from approved RMI corporate registry lists, effectively blocking all future RMI structures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Neglecting to file the Annual Report and pay the franchise tax for two consecutive years, or continuing to operate the boba franchise holding structure for three years after Registrar-issued delinquency notices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registrar strikes the corporation from the register: all corporate powers cease; existing franchise contracts become voidable by franchisees; the name becomes available to third parties; reinstatement requires payment of arrears, penalties, USD 250 reinstatement fee, and a legalized back-filing package.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who contract on behalf of a dissolved corporation are personally liable as principals on every transaction; that liability is joint-and-several and may exceed the corporate net assets, converting a zero-tax structure into unlimited direct exposure to the boba franchise counterparties.
